explore_prose: Every run in this experiment is in the explorer below: filter by outcome to see which settings held the SLOs, or by setting to compare one sweep against another.
Each sweep's hypothesis was written before the runs, and is quoted beside that sweep's measured result below.

hero.html: 78 configurations over 16 sweeps (topology, ep-off, pipeline, moe-collective, moe-collective-wide, kv-capacity, kv-capacity-wide, batch-caps, routing-prefix-cache, prefill-chunking, pd-ratio, pd-always, pd-wide-decode, pd-pool-engine, pd-decode-cudagraph, cudagraph), each at 4 load levels, every run on exactly 64 GPUs.
4x TP8xPP2 + EP, from the pipeline sweep, reached 12.85 tok/s/accelerator (822.5 tok/s across the fleet) at concurrency 128 while holding the scenario's SLOs.
4x TP8xPP2 + EP at concurrency 128. 308 of 312 runs held the SLOs.

meta: deterministic sweep — no LLM in the measurement path
recommendation_prose: The table below ranks the measured operating points by output tok/s per accelerator, the objective this experiment selects on, among runs that held the scenario's SLOs.

prose: Eight single-node TP8 instances should peak highest, since a 64-wide EP group pays cross-node RoCE all-to-all every step for little extra batch.
Measured: best was 4x TP8xDP2 + EP at 6.71 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: topology

prose: Replicating all 256 experts instead of sharding them should cost KV room and throughput against the EP twins in topology.
Measured: best was 4x TP8xDP2 at 4.14 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 64).
sections.title: Sweep: ep-off

prose: Pipeline stages should trail data-parallel shapes of the same width, since each stage adds a boundary hop per decode step.
Measured: best was 4x TP8xPP2 + EP at 12.85 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: pipeline

prose: DeepEP backends should pay off most at cross-node EP width 64, where dispatch crosses RoCE, and matter little at in-node width 8 on NVLink.
Measured: best was 8x TP8 + EP at 4.89 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: moe-collective

prose: At cross-node EP width 64 the DeepEP throughput backends should beat pplx by the most, since every dispatch crosses RoCE.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP8 + EP (all-to-all pplx) at 2.67 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 512).
sections.title: Sweep: moe-collective-wide

prose: fp8 KV should matter most on 8x TP8, whose 80 GiB ranks leave the least KV room (fp8 was +40% there at c=32 in the 8gpu report), and little on the 64-wide DP8 shape.
Measured: best was 8x TP8 + EP (KV dtype fp8) at 6.5 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 64).
sections.title: Sweep: kv-capacity

prose: With the most KV room of any shape, the 64-wide DP8 layout should gain little from fp8 KV or a higher gmu.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP8 + EP (KV dtype fp8) at 2.83 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 512).
sections.title: Sweep: kv-capacity-wide

prose: A seq cap of 32 should bind on 8x TP8 at 512 lanes but not on 2x TP8 DP4, whose dp ranks each schedule their own batch.
Measured: best was 8x TP8 + EP at 4.93 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: batch-caps

prose: prefix-affinity should only beat queue and random with caching on, and eight instances give it the most room to win.
Measured: best was 8x TP8 + EP (prefix caching off) at 4.93 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: routing-prefix-cache

prose: Capping long prefills should trade a little peak throughput for a much lower ITL p99 at saturation.
Measured: best was 8x TP8 + EP at 5.06 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 64).
sections.title: Sweep: prefill-chunking

prose: Decode-heavy ratios should win on AgentX, since cached prefixes leave only a short uncached tail to prefill per turn -- and the RoCE handoff taxes the prefill-heavy splits more.
Measured: best was 4P/4D TP8 + EP at 4.44 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-ratio

prose: Splitting every request should trail the threshold arms, because a turn with a cached prefix pays a cross-node RoCE handoff for little prefill.
Measured: best was 4P/4D TP8 + EP at 4.32 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-always

prose: TP16 decode instances should hold ITL at higher load than TP8 ones, trading batch slots for faster steps.
Measured: best was 6P TP8 + EP / 1D TP16 + EP at 6.08 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-wide-decode

prose: A bigger prefill budget should matter on the prefill-light layout and a decode-pool prefill cap on the decode-heavy one.
Measured: best was 4P/4D TP8 + EP at 4.39 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-pool-engine

prose: Full graph capture on the decode pool should lower ITL by a few percent, with FULL_DECODE_ONLY matching FULL there.
Measured: best was 3P/5D TP8 + EP at 3.72 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-decode-cudagraph

prose: FULL capture should beat the PIECEWISE default by a few percent, and NONE should collapse.
Measured: best was 8x TP8 + EP (graph capture full) at 4.98 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 64).
sections.title: Sweep: cudagraph
